solution_summary: Mount Sinai Health System used Epic on Azure and Azure to modernize a legacy application or infrastructure estate because Mount Sinai Health System needed to migrate their on-premises Epic. Digital channels, integration services, and runtime workloads now sit on managed cloud services instead of brittle legacy infrastructure, making it easier to release changes, add capacity, and keep security or continuity controls close to the platform. The design turns modernization into more than a simple lift-and-shift by combining application hosting, automation, deployment, and data services in one cloud environment that development and operations teams can evolve together. That creates a reusable base for future analytics, service delivery, and resilience improvements while shortening the path from idea to production, and environment to the cloud to keep their hospitals and medical schools at the cutting-edge of care.

evidence_quotes: Mount Sinai Health System needed to migrate their on-premises Epic environment to the cloud to keep their hospitals and medical schools at the cutting-edge of care.
After partnering with Accenture, they chose the Microsoft Azure Cloud to facilitate data collaboration across their workloads and adopt a reference architecture that was purpose-built for Epic.
Now, Mount Sinai can support changes in capacity during events like the pandemic, even as they migrate.
Their internationally acclaimed hospitals innovate across a range of specialties, and their leading medical school educates the next generation of healthcare professionals.
